text: A Markdown checklist of steps in the order they are done. Each step says what starts it, what it changes or moves, where state lives, and what happens if it fails.
Dual writes inside UserRepository: MySQL commits first, then Postgres. A Postgres failure never fails the request and is repaired automatically, with no manual step.
Every copy into Postgres (dual write, backfill, repair) follows the version rule, and the plan shows how a deleted user is prevented from reappearing in Postgres.

The backfill starts only after every instance is dual-writing, allowing for the 30 s flag cache. It reads the MySQL replica in primary-key order, at most 2,000 rows per batch, pauses while replica lag is above 5 s, and resumes after the last completed batch after a crash.
Reads move to Postgres only after a full comparison finds zero mismatches. The source of truth moves only after at least 3 days of 100% Postgres reads.
Reads never fail during the migration. Each change of source of truth (switch or rollback) pauses writes for at most 90 s, with retryable 503s.

Rollback to MySQL without losing any write stays possible until the switch to Postgres-only writes, which happens at least 14 days after Postgres becomes the source of truth. The MySQL table is dropped only after that switch.
